---
title: unauthorized
description: API Reference for the unauthorized function.
version: experimental
related:
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/unauthorized
    - app/api-reference/functions/not-found
    - app/api-reference/functions/forbidden
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts
---

The `unauthorized` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 401 page. It's useful for handling authentication errors, when a request is not signed in. You can customize the UI using the [`unauthorized.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/unauthorized).

Invoking `unauthorized()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;401` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no unauthorized UI renders.

To start using `unauthorized`, enable the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) configuration option in your `next.config.js` file:

```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    authInterrupts: true,
  },
}

export default nextConfig
```

events.content:
Verified: `/admin` returns HTTP 403 with the custom Forbidden page and a `noindex` meta tag, and `/` still returns 200. (The non-zero exit code was just `pkill` terminating the shell that started the server.)

## Summary

The `/admin` page now uses Next.js's built-in auth interrupts, so a non-admin session gets a real `403` status plus a custom error page.

**What I changed**

- `next.config.ts` — enabled `experimental.authInterrupts`, which this Next version requires before `forbidden()`/`unauthorized()` can be used.
- `app/admin/page.tsx` — new server component. It awaits `getSession()` from the existing `app/lib/auth.ts`, calls `unauthorized()` if there's no session (401), calls `forbidden()` if `session.role !== 'admin'` (403), and otherwise renders an "Admin Dashboard" greeting the user by name.
- `app/forbidden.tsx` — the custom 403 page: large "403" heading, "Forbidden" title, a short explanation that the account lacks permission, and a "Return home" link. Placing it at the app root means any future `forbidden()` call anywhere in the app gets the same page.
- `app/unauthorized.tsx` — a matching 401 page for the no-session case, since `getSession()` is typed as nullable. This is a small addition beyond what you asked for; delete it and the `unauthorized()` branch if you'd rather keep it strictly to the 403 path.

**How it was verified**

`tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both pass. I ran `next start` and `curl`ed `/admin`: the response was `HTTP 403`, the body contained the Forbidden page markup and the `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;403` digest, and Next injected `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`.

**One thing to be aware of**

The docs note that the status code is only a real 403 because the role check runs before any streaming starts. If you later wrap the check in `<Suspense>` or turn on Cache Components, the response will already be a 200 by the time `forbidden()` throws — the user still sees the Forbidden UI, but for a true 403 you'd need to move the check into `proxy`.

Side note: `next build` also appended `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `tsconfig.json`'s `include`; that's Next's standard auto-adjustment, not something I edited by hand.
